items.title: Marty Napoleon interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York, New York, January 16, 1999
items.q: So now we’re doing a show and there’s Buster Bailey and Sammy Most.

ctx.x: Oh boy that was great, I loved it. Guys would say to me, “why are you working that dump?” I said, “what do you mean, dump?” You know what I did at the Metropole? Well of course I worked with my own groups, I worked with other people, but I was there for about ten years, different people. And for approximately two and a half years I worked with Charlie Shavers, Coleman Hawkins, Mickey Sheen, and the bass players fluctuated, either Arvell Shaw or Benny Moten, different bass players. But with Charlie Shavers and…

during the night would say “Now we’re going to have — Marty’s going to bring some guys out” and we would get on the floor and do a little bit. People went crazy. So now another country club says hey why don’t we have a New Orleans type of — get that Marty. I did loads of those things. Not only that, I did about ten or twelve weeks on Art Ford’s Channel 13 show, which was coming from Newark, and the only reason they called was because we were at the Metropole, they got most of their guys from the Metropole. Now…
Please write it down so that you don’t have to keep calling back again and again, too, right?
